page: Amazon Web Services c8gn.24xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro System and powered by the 64-bit ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 architecture. It provides 96 dedicated physical cores running at 2.8 GHz without simultaneous multithreading, paired with 192.0 GB of memory to maintain a 1:2 compute-optimized core-to-memory ratio. Network capabilities are substantial, featuring a baseline network bandwidth of 300 Gbps. Local disk storage is not included, meaning all persistent data storage relies on attached Elastic Block Store (EBS) volumes, and no hardware GPUs are present on this server.

Benchmark outcomes demonstrate exceptionally strong multithreaded capacity and memory throughput. Multi-core performance metrics, such as stress-ng and Geekbench multi-core scores, place in the top tier alongside large-block memory read speeds reaching 480.96 GB/sec and write speeds of 218.58 GB/sec. Specialized workloads such as software compilation with Clang, ray tracing, and static web serving throughput also reach top-tier percentiles. In contrast, single-thread performance benchmarks, such as stress-ng single-core and Geekbench single-core, remain in the middle tier, matching the modest 2.8 GHz base clock speed.

The core tradeoff for the c8gn.24xlarge involves its ARM-native software requirement, the absence of local ephemeral storage, and lower single-thread velocity compared to high-frequency x86 alternatives. However, resource density is high across compute and memory channels, and the 300 Gbps network profile enables massive throughput for distributed environments. The c8gn.24xlarge is well positioned for parallel computational tasks, distributed network-heavy architectures, high-concurrency microservices, caching clusters, and extensive multi-threaded CI/CD build farms.
description: Amazon Web Services c8gn.24xlarge is a compute-optimized instance driven by a 96-core AWS Graviton Neoverse-V2 processor utilizing 64-bit ARMv9 architecture at 2.8 GHz. It is provisioned with 192.0 GB of system memory, matching a 1:2 core-to-memory ratio, and operates over the Nitro hypervisor with 300 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. The instance does not include integrated GPUs or local storage drives, requiring EBS volumes for persistent disk storage. Performance evaluations demonstrate top-tier execution across multi-core compute tests, memory bandwidth channels, software compilation, and static web serving, contrasted with average single-core throughput. Given its 96 non-hyperthreaded cores and high network capacity, the c8gn.24xlarge is tailored for parallelized workloads including distributed backend services, high-throughput in-memory caching, large software build pipelines, and multi-threaded data processing.
